findings.evidence: grep for `aFour|ParityOddAssumptions gFour` across the repo returns only ParityOdd.lean:433-518; the sole `ParityOddAssumptions` facts there are `parityOddAssumptions_aOfAlt` (line 355, about `aOfAlt ε K`) and the two defeq-dependent uses at lines 489 and 515. ParityOdd.lean:77 is `public section` with no `@[expose]`.
findings.fix: Add `lemma parityOddAssumptions_aFour : ParityOddAssumptions gFour kFour aFour := parityOddAssumptions_aOfAlt gFour (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)).det (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)) kFour` and use it in `existsUnique_eq_smul_aFour` and `not_isLorentzCovariant_aFour` instead of the unfolded call. This is not the duplicate re-export the earlier reuse finding removed: that one restated a general lemma under a second parameterized name, whereas `aFour` is now a distinct specialized definition whose defining property nothing else states.
findings.issue: No declaration states `ParityOddAssumptions gFour kFour aFour`. The module is `public section` without `@[expose]` (line 77), so `aFour`'s body is hidden and a consumer cannot recover it from `parityOddAssumptions_aOfAlt`. The two in-file users rely on in-module defeq: `existsUnique_eq_smul_aFour` (line 489) and `not_isLorentzCovariant_aFour` (line 515) both pass `parityOddAssumptions_aOfAlt gFour (Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin 4)).det … kFour` at an `aFour`-typed position. Downstream, `aFour` cannot be used as the `A` of `eq_div_smul`, `existsUnique_eq_smul`, `sub_flip_eq_div_smul` or `existsUnique_sub_flip_eq_smul`, all of which take `hA : ParityOddAssumptions g K A`. The module docstring (lines 68-71) advertises `aFour` as 'a non-zero parity-odd tensor', but only `aFour_ne_zero` exists.

summary: The parity-odd API is otherwise complete and well annotated, but `Witness.aFour` ships with no declaration stating that it is parity-odd, and its body is unexposed, so the witness's headline property is unreachable downstream.
